nodes.name: Co-pyrazole complex synthesis
nodes.procedure: 150 mg of Co(OAc)₂·4H₂O (0.847 mmol, Sigma-Aldrich) was dissolved in 50 mL ethanol. To synthesize Co-pyrazole complex, 50 mL of aqueous solution of pyrazole (C₃H₃N₂H, 2.542 mmol (173.1 mg), Sigma-Aldrich) was poured gradually in the above solution at room temperature, then the mixture was stirred for 2 h at 60 °C. The solution was kept overnight without stirring and the Co-pyrazole precipitates were collected through vacuum filtration and dried at 60 °C in an oven.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Co-Pyrazole Complex: First, 150 mg of Co(OAc)₂·4H₂O... dried at 60 °C in an oven.

nodes.name: Co₃O₄–(am-MoSₓ) hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The required amount of Co-pyrazole complex was dispersed and sonicated in an aqueous solution of (NH₄)₂MoS₄ (0.769 mmol (200.1 mg), Sigma-Aldrich) for 1 h. Then, the mixture was transferred into Teflon-lined hydrothermal reactor, heated to 120 °C, and maintained for a required time of 12 h. The black powder of Co₃O₄–(am-MoSₓ) was collected from the vacuum filter and dried at 60 °C in an oven.

nodes.name: Co₉S₈–MoS₂ reductive annealing
nodes.procedure: As-prepared Co₃O₄-(am-MoSₓ) was transferred into an alumina boat and annealed in a tubular furnace at a required temperature (300-500 °C) for 2 h in H₂ environment.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Co₉S₈–MoS₂ Heterostructure: As-prepared Co₃O₄-(am-MoSₓ)... annealed... at 400 °C for 2 h in H₂ environment.

nodes.name: Co₉S₈–MoS₂/NF electrode fabrication
nodes.procedure: Ni foam was sonicated first in ethanol followed by acetone for 30 min and then treated with 3.0 M HCl to remove oxide layer and washed several times with distilled water. The precleaned nickel foam was dip-coated in the ink of as-synthesized Co₃O₄–(am-MoSₓ) and dried at 60 °C in an oven. The Co₉S₈–MoS₂/NF (1.2 mg cm⁻²) electrode was obtained after reduction of Co₃O₄–(am-MoSₓ)/NF at 400 °C for 2 h in H₂ environment.

nodes.name: Co₉S₈ single phase synthesis
nodes.procedure: 100 mg of Co(OAc)₂·4H₂O (0.565 mmol, Sigma-Aldrich) and 860 mg of thiourea (SC(NH₂)₂, 11.298 mmol, Sigma-Aldrich) were dissolved in 50 mL of distilled water with stirring for 2 h. The solution was heated hydrothermally at 180 °C for 12 h. Then, the powder was prepared by vacuum filtering and dried at 60 °C in an oven. The powder was reduced at 400 °C for 2 h in H₂ to obtain reduced Co₉S₈.

nodes.procedure: (NH₄)₆Mo₇O₂₄·4H₂O (0.405 mmol (500 mg), Sigma-Aldrich) with 1.232 g of thiourea (16.183 mmol, Sigma-Aldrich) in hydrothermal reactor and the reductive annealing was followed as well.

nodes.characterization_summary: The (002) peak of MoS2 shifts from 14.4° to 12.9° and the (311) peak of cubic Co9S8 shifts from 29.9° to 29.7°, confirming deformation in both crystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The main (002) peak of MoS2 is slightly shifted from 2θ = 14.4° to 12.9°, and the (311) peak of cubic Co9S8 shows a minor shift from 29.9° to 29.7°.

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern with multiple phases

nodes.characterization_summary: Lower intensities and broadness of E2g¹ than A1g signals reveal defects in MoS2; A1g peak red shifts to 399.5 cm⁻¹; Δω reduced to 23.33 cm⁻¹ indicating fewer MoS2 layers; Co9S8 shows blue shift to 678.1 cm⁻¹ indicating strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lower intensities and broadness of E2g¹ than A1g signals of MoS2 in the Co9S8–MoS2 heterostructure reveals the presence of defects in MoS2 ... a blue shift is observed in characteristic band of Co9S8 (678.1 cm⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p shows Co–S peaks at 778.4 and 793.4 eV; Mo 3d shows Mo–S doublet at 228.2 and 231.3 eV; positive shift in Co–S and negative shift in Mo–S indicate electron transfer from Co to Mo; S defects confirmed by reduced S 2s peak area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co–S peaks at 778.4 and 793.4 eV increase remarkably in Co 2p spectra for Co9S8–MoS2 ... the positive shift in Co–S peaks (778.38/793.38 to 778.40/793.40 eV) and the negative shift in Mo–S peaks (228.78/231.88 to 228.20/231.3 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge shifts to higher energy indicating slight oxidation of Co from Co1.78+ to Co1.78+δ; Mo K-edge matches reference MoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K absorption edge of Co9S8–MoS2 shifts toward the higher energy compared to pristine Co9S8, demonstrating the slight oxidation of cobalt from Co1.78+ to Co1.78+δ.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge shows increased intensity at 1.5-2.5 Å from Co–S and Co–Co bonds; Mo K-edge shows Mo–S at 1.93 Å and Mo–Mo at 2.82 Å with decreased Mo–S intensity and increased Debye–Waller factor for Mo–S.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS spectrum of Co9S8–MoS2 at 1.5-2.5 Å ... originating from the combined scatterings of Co–S and Co–Co bonds has increased intensity ... Slightly decreased intensity for Mo–S peak.

nodes.characterization_summary: Porous supraparticular assembly structure with pore size ≈200 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co3O4–(am-MoSx) displays a porous supraparticular assembly structure with a pore size of ≈500 nm, which decreases to ≈200 nm upon reductive annealing to make Co9S8–MoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co9S8 nanoparticles on MoS2 basal plane show crystal planes (311), (111), (222), and (440).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The (311), (111), (222), and (440) crystal planes and corresponding FFT of Co9S8 nanoparticle formed on the MoS2 sheets are confirmed by high-resolution scan.

nodes.characterization_summary: Line-scan confirms successful growth of Co9S8 NPs on MoS2 sheet forming 0D–2D heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The compositional line-scan profile of Co9S8–MoS2 ... shows successful growth of Co9S8 NPs on the MoS2 sheet to form 0D–2D heterostructure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform elemental distribution of Co, Mo, S throughout the particle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) maps of Co9S8–MoS2 (Figure 3g–j) demonstrate uniform elemental distribution throughout the particle.
